Guided walkthrough of every tab in the Lancer Automations configuration window.
Walks through the Activation Manager dialog (custom activations, defaults, startup scripts).

The gameplay tools inside the Token Action HUD: skirmish/barrage, boost, deploy, contest, scan, link, reinforcement, downtime, reserve, vote.

Coding and automation can feel rough, and mid-game you need stuff fast. Here's a UI on top of the Lancer Automations systems, no code.
The standard effect page. Pick a status, a duration, optionally an auto-consume trigger.
Pick a status and a stack count. Target is up top.
How long it sticks: end/start of turn, indefinite, etc.
Optional auto-consume trigger (on hit, on damage, on turn end...). Picking some triggers reveals extra filters: item LID, action name, status, check type.
Save a filled-in effect as a preset and reload it later - handy for ones you apply often.

Registering every possible status from NPC stuff is tedious and noisy on the status list. This tab lets you create temporary statuses on the fly. With my temporary-custom-statuses module some can be saved and reused.
Name, icon, duration, note. Same shape as Standard but for ad-hoc statuses.
Statuses saved through temporary-custom-statuses show up here for reuse, and on a separate Statuses tab in TAH.

The advanced stuff, and one of the core features of the Lancer Automations engine. Many many things go through here: accuracy, damage on next attack, immunities, rerolls, target modifiers. They inject into the regular Lancer system cards seamlessly. Read doc/API_EFFECTS.md for the full menu.
The bonus type. Each one reveals its own fields below.
Same trigger picker as Standard. Combined with Uses, this is how you build things like 3 stacks of +1d6 damage on next attack, consumed on damage roll.
Adds the bonus to the target.
Everything currently on a token, including passive bonuses you can't see otherwise (Veterancy adding a passive on a HASE check, etc.).
Add extras and effects to any actor or item right from its sheet. The L.A button in its header is the entry point; the number shows how much is already attached.

The L.A button opens this menu. Add Effect opens the Effect Manager for this sheet, Add Extra attaches actions/deployables/bars, and Extra Config (items only) tunes auto-consume and deployable range/count.
Add Extra opens this: tie extra actions, deployables, and resource bars onto the actor or item.
Custom actions bolted onto the actor or item - name, activation, icon, optional resource limits. They show up in the TAH.
Attach deployables by actor or LID, or drag one in - this is how an NPC feature gets its deployable in the TAH. The T1/T2/T3 pills gate an entry to that NPC tier; none lit = every tier.
Quick-add a manual token stat bar to track anything you like.
Actions can also be an attack or damage roll.
Re-open this any time from the Lancer Automations button in the Game Settings sidebar, under the LANCER section.

Pretty simple, here's the configuration menu where all the Lancer Automations options live. Note: some settings are client-side (per user) and not shared world-wide (Token Action HUD, custom stat bars, vision debug overlays, etc.). Each player must enable them on their own client.
Every page groups related stuff, sorted by family on the left. The search box up top looks through all of them at once.
How activation popups feel during play: who sees them, whether the reaction is auto-spent, and a couple of niche toggles.
All the combat-flavor toggles: knockback, throw, movement-cap, boost detection, alt structure/stress rules, infection damage. The big stuff.
What happens when something dies. Spawn a wreck token, play the explosion, optionally drop terrain. Per-category if you want monstrosity wrecks to look different from mech wrecks.
Half-size tokens, auto wall-height for tokens, my own token stat bars (a Bar Brawl alternative). Mostly QoL display tweaks.
Fixes for isometric modules (Isometric Perspective, Grape Juice). Only shows when one is active.
Here you can enable the TAH, my own Token Action HUD. It offers a bunch of tools, with UI and sound, and a few options to tune it. Still work in progress but fairly usable.
All the sound feedback options, including the UI sounds for the TAH.
The FX section: status visual effects (glows, shaders) plus the extra statuses I added. A bit like Lancer QoL, so pick one or the other if both are on.
Flip these on if something feels off and you want to see what the module is doing under the hood.
My optional content packs (personal stuff), the News & Releases history, and one-shot maintenance buttons: LCP repair, reset, export, import.
Vision-from-edge for big tokens, the Lancer Sensors and Battlefield Awareness detection modes (auto-add, combat-only, range source), basic-sight overrides, and drag-vision behavior all live here.
Re-run the Setup Wizard, or launch any tour: Token Action HUD, ruler & movement, advanced measure, effect manager, automation. They can run long - start one now or come back whenever.

Where you build automations. Item-bound (per LID) or general, code-driven, fired on triggers like onMove, onHit, onActivation, and so on.
Custom is your own stuff. Defaults are the activations bundled with the module. Startup is JS that runs once on Foundry ready.
Your activations, grouped into folders. Each row binds to one or more triggers and runs your code.
Create a new one. You'll pick item-bound (LID) or general, the triggers, and the code blocks that run on evaluate / activate / init.
Add opens this editor. Triggers, filters, and code all live here; Save commits, closing discards.
Bind it to an item (by LID) or make it general - checked on every token.
For item-bound activations, the item's Lancer ID. The finder button beside it searches your items and compendiums, so you don't type it by hand.
Tick the triggers that fire it: onMove, onHit, onActivation, onStructure, and many more.
Narrow when it fires: react to self or others, disposition, in or out of combat, auto-activate.
Your logic: evaluate (should it fire?), activation (what happens), plus onInit and onMessage.
The editor suggests API names as you type. Press Alt-Enter to open the list, then arrow through to see what each does.
Make folders to keep things tidy. Drag rows in to file them.
Filter by name, LID, or trigger type. Handy when the list gets long.
The activations bundled with the module: Overwatch, Brace, Flight, Fall, plus a bunch of NPC-feature automations. Toggle them on or off.
JS that runs once on Foundry ready. Good for helper functions you want your activations to reuse.
The Lancer Automations Token Action HUD - your token's action menu.
Click the name to open the actor sheet.
Unlock with the lock icon, then drag the HUD anywhere. The reset icon restores its position.
Click the swords icon to add or remove the token from the combat tracker without leaving the HUD.
Live vitals: HP, heat, structure and stress pips, overshield, burn.
Click to expand armor, evasion, e-defense, tech attack, save, sensors, and core.
The right number is the max move this turn (speed); the left is what the token has used so far. Boost (or anything granting extra move) extends the cap.

Quick / Full / Reaction / Protocol / Move pips. Click to spend, right-click to restore; on your turn the spent slot becomes End Turn. It mirrors Lancer\'s own action tracker, so you can disable that one in the Lancer system settings.
Revert the last move, or clear this token\'s recorded history.
Drive the HUD by keyboard: Shift+WASD moves, Shift+E left-clicks, Shift+Q right-clicks, Shift+F searches.
The Menu column lists categories (Actions, Weapons, Systems, Frame, Talents, Utility, Statuses). Hovering or clicking a row cascades extra columns out to the right.
Any row that is not a sub-category is an item. Left-click usually activates it; right-click (or Shift+Q) opens a detail popup with its full text.
A coloured triangle on a row's left edge marks it automated - using it runs its built-in effects.
Right-click any item (or Shift+Q) to open a detail popup: full text, tags, and any Disable / Destroy toggles.
Click the magnifier or press Shift+F to live-filter every action.
Ctrl+Right-click any action to pick which wheel it goes on. The mark on a row says where it lives. Hover the star tab to open the list.

Press F on a selected token: your favorites form a wheel around it. Click an icon to use it, right-click for its details, hover for the range preview. Tab switches to the second wheel once you have one.
Press G for the statuses on the token plus the ones starred in the status panel. Click to apply or add a stack, right-click to remove one. Removing a permanent effect asks first.
Sub-categories of tools: Gameplay actions, Movement helpers, Measures (the Advanced Measure tool), Log, Glossary, and a Misc grab-bag.
There is a lot more under the hood, but the tour would get long. Drop by Discord if you have questions.
A pass through the tools tucked into the HUD, past just firing weapons.
That's the toolbox. Dig through Utility for the rest.
Drag a token to measure. The ruler follows Lancer rules: speed cap, terrain cost, climb, flight ceiling.
Press M on a selected token to open this wheel and set its base movement type - walk, fly, drift, each with its own cost rules.
During a drag, press M to cycle the type for that drag only - the token's base type stays put.
Hold V for free movement (no cost, ignores terrain). Hold B for debug movement (skips automation hooks). Ctrl+drag from empty space gives the vanilla ruler.
Force is unintentional movement (knockback, drag): it doesn't trigger move automations like Overwatch.
A measuring toolset reusing LA's targeting visuals - toggle it with Shift+R. Everything lives on this floating toolbar.
Hover here for the full cheat-sheet. Quick ones: Ctrl+wheel rotate, Shift+wheel size, Q/E elevation, W/S tilt a line, Z reset.
Pick a shape - Blast, Burst, Cone, Line - or a single Target mark. Options make it 3D (elevation), auto-follow terrain, and propagate cell to cell.
Pulse a range around the shape: a manual radius, threat, sensor, max reach, or a weapon's range. T cycles sources, re-clicking the active one turns it off. A movement-reach toggle is here too.

Right-click a range source (or a weapon in its list) to pin it: a steady ring that stays while the tool is open, on as many tokens as you want. Pinned entries show a ★; the TAH range toggles pin the same way.
Shift+click in free mode marks a token (shows its range and reach) or the ground (manual-range only). Hold Ctrl for the vanilla Measure Distance ruler.
